To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the design and synthesis led to a series of pyrrolidine derivatives with low nanomolar activity against nNOS and high selectivity over eNOS, which can be further optimized by the introduction of a fluorine atom into the 3' position.

the design and synthesis led to the discovery and characterization of low nanomole nNOS inhibitors with more than 1,000 fold selectivity for the enzyme over eNOS and that the binding of 4 to nNOS revealed a unique binding mode that is the same as that for the inhibitor 3, which is the result of enzyme elasticity to generate an additional binding pocket.
we have designed and synthesized a novel series of pyrrolinomethyl 4 aminopyridines as nNOS inhibitors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and synthesis, as well as the structural elucidation, of a series of pyrrolidine derivatives with potent nNOS inhibitory activity.
the discovery of nNOS inhibitors and the exploration of the active site for ligands binding, which may provide useful information for the design and development of nNOS specific inhibitors.
the development of nNOS inhibitors with the goal of discovering novel agents to treat neurodegenerative diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a trans substituted amino pyridine moiety is the key pharmacophore for nNOS inhibitors, and the pyrrolidino moiety can induce enzyme elasticity, which is important for nNOS inhibition.

the NOS active-site cavity is a dynamic structure and that ligand binding can induce conformational changes in the active site, which may provide new insights into the development of more potent nNOS inhibitors and other enzyme targets.
the pyrrolidino moiety of the ligand is the key structural element that determines the binding mode of the ligand to the enzyme.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the design and synthesis strategy for NOS inhibitors can be used to develop new therapeutic agents to treat various neurological disorders.
the NOS active sites are very flexible and can accommodate various ligand binding modes.
the active site of nNOS can be explored by the design and syntheses of various pyrrolidinoethyl 2 amino pyridine derivatives.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the binding mode of 4 can be induced by the cis/trans isomerization of the pyrrolidino ring, which provides an effective strategy to design and synthesize nNOS inhibitors.
the design and synthesis strategy we used can be applied to other NOS inhibitors to optimize binding interactions and to improve the pharmacokinetic properties.
a cis conformation of the pyrrolidino ring is essential for the binding of the inhibitors to the active site of nNOS.
